requirement.evidence: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
requirement.note: Relocation assistance also stated: 'If your landlord evicts you for certain reasons, they might have to help pay for your moving costs.'

status.evidence: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you.

citation.evidence: Both landlords and tenants may submit official petitions to request rent adjustments, report violations, or contest unauthorized pass-through costs. Our impartial hearing process ensures all parties are treated fairly under the Ordinance.
citation.note: The page refers to the Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance generally, but gives no section number. The citation is only the ordinance name.

requirement.evidence: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
requirement.note: The cap, the 2.87% figure for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027, and the Tenant Petition option are all stated. But the page does not say that rent can be raised only once a year. It says 'each year', which is looser.

key_value.evidence: 2.87 percent is the maximum allowable rent increase for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.
key_value.note: The lesser-of 3% or 80% CPI rule is stated in the Rent Increase Limits section.
